what: The invariants the property suites state, one row each. Every suite is deterministic: a fixed seed and numRuns.
why: A property suite that nothing lists can be deleted without anyone noticing, and an invariant with no suite is a sentence. scripts/lib/property-invariants.test.mjs fails when a listed file is missing, when an invariant has no describe block, and when a *.property.test.ts exists unlisted.

invariants.statement: No illegal job transition is accepted: canTransition/transition agree with an independently stated table on every ordered pair, and are total (never throw) over foreign state strings.
invariants.shownToFail: A seeded wrong claim is refuted; mutating the transition table (succeeded -> queued) fails 7 tests.

invariants.statement: Terminal job states absorb: no edge leaves succeeded, failed, cancelled or expired under any fence, and every state can reach a terminal state.
invariants.shownToFail: Mutating the table to give succeeded an outgoing edge fails the suite.

invariants.statement: A caller whose fencing token is not the current one is refused as fenced_out before legality is consulted, and never moves a job.
invariants.shownToFail: The 4-vs-5 example pins a token newer than the store's.

invariants.statement: deriveRunState keeps phase, outcome and status consistent: terminal exactly when outcome is set, a payload has no authority over a non-complete outcome, status is passed only for a complete run that says passed.
invariants.shownToFail: Letting a non-terminal phase keep the claimed outcome fails 2 tests.

invariants.statement: planEventBatch accepts nothing new after the run has ended: a terminal event followed by anything refuses the whole batch as terminal_event.
invariants.shownToFail: Deleting the terminal check in planEventBatch fails 3 tests.

invariants.statement: Replaying an accepted batch is idempotent (all duplicates, still ready) and the same event id with different content is a hash mismatch.
invariants.shownToFail: Covered by the same mutation run as RUN-1 and the seeded wrong-claim test.

invariants.statement: New events in a ready plan are contiguous from the expected sequence, and a gap is refused whole as sequence_gap.
invariants.shownToFail: Covered by the seeded wrong-claim test.

invariants.statement: executeWithRetry makes at most retries + 1 calls, never retries a non-idempotent operation or a permanent status, and retries a known rejection within the same budget.
invariants.shownToFail: Found no defect; the seeded wrong-claim test proves the generators reach deep budgets.

invariants.statement: Every executeWithRetry backoff lies in [100, MAX_RETRY_BACKOFF_MS] and never decreases. FOUND A DEFECT: the schedule had no ceiling (MNT-100).
invariants.shownToFail: Run with the cap removed, the suite fails with counterexample [10, 408]; examples pin retries 30 and 40.

invariants.statement: isRetryableStatus is true exactly for the listed transient statuses and false for no status.
invariants.shownToFail: Examples pin 500, 499 and 0.

invariants.statement: The runner spool backoff delay is an integer in [1, maxDelayMs] for every configurable policy, attempt and random draw, and the first delay is within [base/2, base].
invariants.shownToFail: Removing the maxDelayMs clamp fails 3 tests.

invariants.statement: The spool backoff is monotone in the attempt count for a fixed draw and is pinned at the maximum once the exponential passes it.
invariants.shownToFail: Covered by the same clamp mutation.

invariants.statement: The default spool retry policy lies inside the configurable domain.
invariants.shownToFail: Example-style check; the seeded wrong-claim test covers the harness.

invariants.statement: JUnit parse -> normalise preserves counts: passed + failed + skipped + flaky equals the number of testcases, each count matches the generating model, and attempt indexes are 1..n per test id.
invariants.shownToFail: Removing the <error> rung from the status ladder fails 2 tests.

invariants.statement: The run status follows the ladder (failed > skipped-only > flaky > passed) and a document cut short never reports a pass nor claims completeness.
invariants.shownToFail: Covered by the same mutation run.

invariants.statement: Parsing is total for junit, playwright, k6, zap and legacy-upload: arbitrary bytes, JSON-shaped input and markup yield a contract-valid result or a classified Error.
invariants.shownToFail: Found no defect; examples pin null entries and empty containers.

invariants.statement: Well-formed XML with no testcase is refused with a classified error, never reported as a pass.
invariants.shownToFail: Seeded wrong-claim test covers the harness.

invariants.statement: Appending the same outbox event again is a no-op: one row, the same sequence and event id, and the second append reports no insert; batches with repeats leave one row per distinct key in first-seen order.
invariants.shownToFail: Seeded wrong-claim test ("a repeated key adds a row") is refuted.

invariants.statement: A read bound to workspace A never returns workspace B rows, even when dedupe keys collide across workspaces; the retention floor is per workspace.
invariants.shownToFail: Removing the workspace filter from readAfter fails 4 of 6 tests.

invariants.statement: A malformed append (blank workspace, empty or over-long dedupe key) is refused before it touches the table.
invariants.shownToFail: Covered by the harness test.

invariants.statement: Adding an open finding never raises the overall health score or any dimension's score.
invariants.shownToFail: The harness test asserts the opposite claim (an added critical raises the score) and is refuted.

invariants.statement: While any enabled hard gate is tripped, the overall score is at or below GATE_CEILING and the letter is D or F.
invariants.shownToFail: Disabling the cap in compute() fails the property on its first generated input.

invariants.statement: An opt-in dimension (delivery, ai-governance, test-effectiveness, agent-quality, accessibility) changes nothing in the grade until a policy weights it: adding any opt-in issue finding, tool or metric leaves the score, letter, limiter, gates and fix-next identical.
invariants.shownToFail: Run before DEFAULT_HEALTH_WEIGHTS carried the five keys, the suite failed on its first input (a secret filed under delivery tripped the gate) and the harness test refutes the claim with the opt-in dimensions weighted.

invariants.statement: Adding an `OR <allowed id>` branch to a licence expression never turns it from allowed into denied; the widened expression is always allowed.
invariants.shownToFail: Making OR take the worse branch fails the property; the harness test refutes a wrong claim.

invariants.statement: `A AND B` (and `B AND A`) is denied whenever A alone is denied.
invariants.shownToFail: Making AND take the better operand fails the property.

invariants.statement: Parsing the formatted text of a licence expression returns the same expression.
invariants.shownToFail: Dropping the parentheses around compound operands in formatLicenceExpression fails the round trip.

invariants.statement: An empty diff, or one with no executable changed line, has diff coverage null — never 100%.
invariants.shownToFail: Returning 1 for an empty denominator fails the property.

invariants.statement: Marking one more changed executable line covered never lowers diff coverage.
invariants.shownToFail: Counting covered lines outside the diff fails the property.

invariants.statement: parseUnifiedDiff recovers exactly the added new-file line numbers of a generated diff, with LF or CRLF, even when hunk content looks like a header.
invariants.shownToFail: Reading `+++` lines inside a hunk as headers fails the property.

invariants.statement: Covered never exceeds executable, the ratio lies in [0, 1], and the uncovered lines listed are exactly executable minus covered.
invariants.shownToFail: Covered by the harness test.

invariants.statement: Renaming volatile tokens (numbers, UUIDs, hex, paths, timestamps, quoted data) never changes a failure's signature or the clustering.
invariants.shownToFail: Found a real defect while written: a path starting with `-/` was split in two. That input is pinned as an example.

invariants.statement: Two different root-cause templates never share a signature, whatever fills their volatile slots.
invariants.shownToFail: Emptying every quoted string, including the property after `reading`, merges two templates and fails the property.

invariants.statement: A test whose decisive results are all failures is never suggested for quarantine, at any threshold.
invariants.shownToFail: Removing the broken-not-flaky filter in suggestQuarantine fails the property.

invariants.statement: Raising minScore never adds quarantine suggestions.
invariants.shownToFail: Covered by the harness test.

invariants.statement: A flaky score lies in [0, 1], is 0 for a test with no flaky or passed result, and does not depend on other tests' observations.
invariants.shownToFail: Covered by the harness test.

invariants.statement: Change failure rate and rework rate are always in [0, 1] or null, in the current and the previous window.
invariants.shownToFail: The harness test refutes values of 1.0000001 and -0.1 with fc.check.

invariants.statement: Adding a successful production deployment that ships no new change and is not a rollback, hotfix or unplanned deployment never raises the change failure rate.
invariants.shownToFail: Blaming a rollback on the immediately previous deployment fails the property; that counterexample is pinned.

invariants.statement: A DORA metric resting on fewer observations than minSample is insufficient, with no value and no band.
invariants.shownToFail: Removing the sample floor fails the property.

invariants.statement: Every cycle-time phase and the review latency satisfy 0 <= min <= median <= p75 <= max, or are all null for an empty sample.
invariants.shownToFail: Removing the coding-time clamp fails the property.

invariants.statement: Every directory's bus factor is between 1 and its author count.
invariants.shownToFail: An off-by-one bus factor fails the property.

invariants.statement: Adding a matching AI-agent signal to a commit or pull request never lowers the attribution confidence.
invariants.shownToFail: fc.check refutes a classifier that scores only the winning mode's signals; a defect in the suite's own injector is pinned as an example.

invariants.statement: A subject with no author identity and no signal is never classified human.
invariants.shownToFail: fc.check refutes a classifier that maps unknown to human.

invariants.statement: A pull request attributed to a human is never subject to the AI-governance rules, under any policy.
invariants.shownToFail: fc.check refutes a gate that applies its rules to everyone.

invariants.statement: An identical baseline and candidate eval run is never a fail, for any run and any comparison seed.
invariants.shownToFail: Comparing candidate.high <= baseline.high fails EVAL-1 and EVAL-2; the harness test refutes 'any candidate never fails' with a pinned 10/10 → 0/10 example.

invariants.statement: A candidate eval run whose every attempt passes never fails against any baseline.
invariants.shownToFail: Adding 0.05 to the allowance fails the pinned 5000-attempt perfect baseline against a 1-attempt perfect candidate.

invariants.statement: For every agent, model and the overall row, p50 run latency never exceeds p95, and both are null together.
invariants.shownToFail: Swapping p50 and p95 fails the property.

invariants.statement: Adding a span with no matching price never changes the known cost total or the priced-span count; only the unknown count rises, by one if the span is billable.
invariants.shownToFail: Billing an invoke_agent span when nothing else in its trace has tokens fails the property with a shrunk counterexample.

invariants.statement: Every detected tool-call loop has at least max(2, threshold) consecutive execute_tool spans with the loop's tool name and argument hash.
invariants.shownToFail: Hard-coding the threshold to 2 fails the property.

invariants.statement: Every rendering of a scheduled report fits its platform limit at any limit from 80 characters up (Telegram, Slack, plain text for WhatsApp and Signal), and a report never shows more than three items, with the rest counted, nor more than three area lines or three actions, with no action listed twice.
invariants.shownToFail: Dropping the link-length reservation in renderTelegram fails the limit property on a long link.

invariants.statement: Telegram HTML and Slack mrkdwn are always well escaped: with the renderer’s own tags removed no < or > remains and every & begins an entity, including where a line was trimmed to fit.
invariants.shownToFail: The harness refutes an unescaped renderer in the suite itself; trimming the escaped text instead of the raw text cuts & and fails the pinned examples.
